title: Mass predictions from knot formulas vs. CODATA/PDG values
html:
Remark. Mass predictions from knot formulas vs. CODATA/PDG values

This table evaluates the topological knot formulas (knot formula table) at the substrate parameter q_0. We derive q_0 from the muon--electron mass ratio (Skein mass relation). We compare the results against CODATA 2022 recommended values and PDG 2024 averages. All masses are in MeV/c^2.

Input parameters (one free parameter):

  q = q_0, \quad
  \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} = 0.09905, \quad
  \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2.02988.

Table 2: Predicted vs.\ observed masses.

Leptons (from Skein volume).

See Table 1.

The electron mass is an input. It fixes \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} through the pair Skein mass. The muon mass prediction equals \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2. This reproduces the CODATA value to six significant figures at q = q_0.

Hadrons (from pair Skein masses).

The proton and neutron rows derive from the LO \rho_K assembly (witness: atomic-mass-via-rho-k.witness.json). This assembly consumes m_p and m_n as CODATA inputs. It is tautological by construction. The |\mathrm{tr}_M| factor cancels in \rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}} \cdot m_e \cdot |\mathrm{tr}_M|, reducing the output to Z m_p + N m_n. The FULL framework prediction requires the unified knot mass formula M(\mathfrak{H}) = \rho \cdot [|\mathrm{tr}_M(T_w)| + \mathrm{tower}(T_w) + \mathrm{tr}_M(C_{\dim_q})]. This formula does not yet extend to the nucleon scale. The n–p splitting emerges as a consequence of the FULL \mathfrak{Q}_\beta chain (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta + m_e \approx 1.293 MeV).

See Table 2.

† Tautological under the LO chain. The proton, neutron, and n-p split rows return the CODATA inputs because the LO formula collapses to Z m_p + N m_n (no binding correction).

FULL \mathfrak{Q}_\beta prediction (framework, no CODATA mass injection)

Per prop:neutron-qvalue-symbolic, the framework predicts the \beta-decay Q-value using only CAL-1 (m_e) and CAL-2 (q_0):

\boxed{
\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\text{pred}} = \frac{m_e \cdot |q_0^2 - 2q_0 - 1| \cdot (q_0 + 1)}{2 q_0^3} \approx 0.7836 \text{ MeV}
}

This compares to the CODATA value of 0.7823 MeV (+0.168\% error, +1.31 keV). At single wrap, the L_\pm and e^- contributions cancel exactly between proton and neutron. Thus \Delta(\mathrm{net}) = h(h-2)/2 with h = q_0 - q_0^{-1}. The entire Q-value lies in the \gamma + \sigma_0 + \sigma_1 channels.

The n-p mass split follows: \mathfrak{m}_n - \mathfrak{m}_p = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta + m_e \approx 1.295 MeV. This compares to the CODATA value of 1.293 MeV (0.17\% error, no CODATA m_n - m_p input).

The +1.31 keV residual stems from the brane-tower truncation. The derived E_0 uses the single-level Planck-tick approximation. The exact tower-summed E_0 corrects this. The typed-crossings 6-term form yields a looser prediction of 0.7882 MeV (+0.747\% error). We keep this in the witness for cross-checks. Witness: q-beta-predicted.witness.json.

Light nuclei (from multi-body Skein).

All rows below come from the LO \rho_K assembly using CODATA m_p, m_n inputs. The \Delta column equals the CODATA binding energy by construction. The FULL multi-body unified knot mass formula at H_{3A} remains intractable beyond A = 1. Binding-energy predictions require resolving the open \Delta_\lambda research question (see recomputed-low-isotope-mass-table.md:99).

See Table 3.

† LO output is constituent sum only. The full prediction (beyond the constituent sum) is not yet available. Witness: atomic-mass-via-rho-k.witness.json.

Notes. The muon--electron mass ratio fixes the substrate parameter q. Hadronic masses follow from the pair Skein formula (terminal resolution). Nuclear binding follows from the Hopf-junction Skein change \Delta E = \Delta\mathcal{S}. We evaluate the multi-body Skein polynomials up to {}^4\mathrm{He}. Polynomials beyond A = 4 are computable in principle (embeddability closure) but remain unevaluated.

Sources and scope. The proton and neutron entries use CODATA 2022 values directly. The nuclear entries use AME2020 binding energies. These entries recombine observed constants. The parameter q predicts mass ratios (m_\mu/m_e = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2), Q-values (\Delta\mathrm{net} \times E_0), and half-life ratios via \log_q(ft) spectroscopy. The single external scaling ruler is m_e = 0.510999\;\text{MeV} MeV (CODATA 2022 input). This ruler converts dimensionless q-ratios to physical MeV.

Isotope-level data (hecke-engine certificates, A \leq 14).

The hecke-engine provides exact Skein polynomial evaluations at q_0 for 47 isotopes from {}^2\mathrm{H} through {}^{60}\mathrm{Co}. All 47 isotopes have corresponding AME2020 binding-energy data. The certificate fields encode combinatorial crossing structure, not mass directly.

See Table 4.

The F_{\mathrm{Pauli}} factor remains O(1) across all isotopes and encodes the Pauli exclusion statistical weight. The \ln|P| column records the transfer matrix Skein polynomial evaluated at q_0. Neither field maps linearly to B/A or mass in MeV. See certificate-to-mass.witness.json for validation.
